title: cli: the os migrate apply drop-gate refusal prescribes os migrate organization-ownership, which 18.0 refuses NOT_IMPLEMENTED — the remedy dead-ends
body:
QA-source: #24556 · cli.organization-ownership-ceremony · acceptance[3]

Found by the 18.0 release QA sweep (subject `5b14b7f3`); also recorded in #24558 (the item is in both selectors). The clause itself passes (the drop gate refuses without a verified marker and applies once one is planted); this card is about the refusal's prescription.

## What is wrong

`os migrate apply --allow-destructive` on a 17.x-created database refuses the column drop and tells the operator to run `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`, review it, then `--apply --plan-file PLAN` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts:589`). In 18.0 that command is withdrawn: it refuses every arm with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` ("fresh installs only", `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_UPGRADE_UNAVAILABLE_CODE`, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts:1107-1115`). So the remedy the refusal names cannot be run. The boot guard's own refusal already hedges ("keep this one on a 17.x release until…"); the drop-gate text does not. The command's own help example (`organization-ownership.ts:332`, `os migrate organization-ownership --out plans/v18-ownership.json`) has the same problem.

## Reproduction

1. Create a database with `@objectstack/cli@17.7.0` (`objectstack start -d file:V17.db --auth-secret …`, one sign-up), stop it, copy it.
2. With the 18.0 CLI: `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes --database-url file:COPY.db` → refusal naming `os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN`.
3. Run the named command → refused `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

Expected: the drop-gate refusal states what 18.0 actually supports for this database (the same position the boot guard states), not a withdrawn command.

Severity: low (message accuracy — AGENTS.md "runtime strings carry the lesson"), but it is on the 18.0 upgrade path an operator hits first.
